steps.text: Grazie infinite, Signor Bellone!
I would've been at such a loss, had it not been for you and your famiglia.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Come now, Zio Elio. I didn't do anything.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Indeed, your name and presence were enough.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: My landlord dropping by as you were visiting me was enough to make him reconsider collecting his rent on the spot.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: After you left, he quickly agreed to give me two more weeks. That I'll figure out myself...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I don't understand, Zio Elio. Why are you...? What happened to your fruit stand?

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Oh, that? Hah. Sold it long ago.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: My little Emma had a fever this summer, and who would have thought it would leave her paralyzed?

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Luckily, Demetri introduced me to a good doctor, said it was a serious yet common summer ailment for children, and she might lose her legs if it wasn't treated.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: So I sold my fruit stand, and pooled cash from relatives to pay part of the doctor's fees. The rest is to be paid in installments.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: She's out of the woods now, at least. She has a slight limp, but she's otherwise healthy. As for the rent and bills... I'll figure it out.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Your stand was on the corner... Metri and I bought oranges from you when we were little.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: We've been neighbors for years. I could've lent you some money, and you wouldn't have had to—

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: No, no, Signor Bellone. It's a vast sum, I wouldn't dare accept such a favor from you.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Besides, your money wouldn't keep me afloat forever. I owe rent every week.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: But now that I'm under Famiglia Bellone's protection... my landlord won't kick me out when I fail to pay; and even the bakery will sell me some food on credit.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But... you never wanted to join the Famiglia.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You always said there was no need for civilians to join or involve themselves in famiglie affairs—that the most important thing was to work hard and live your best life.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Ha! This old man was just naive.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: A famiglia is more than fighting and killing. I finally understand that.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Don't worry, Signor Bellone. I may be old, but I know not to be ungrateful.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: The Bellones have helped me, so if you ever need a favor in turn, just call me and I'll be there!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...You did this on purpose, didn't you? Metri.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I asked you the other day why I haven't seen his fruit stand, and you told me he went home for a relative's funeral.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You knew Emma was gravely ill.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And when you suddenly invited me here for pizza the other day... you knew Zio Elio would pass by and find me.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You handled it expertly, Leon.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Handled what? I played right into your hands, if I had known sooner—

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: —You couldn't have done anything about it anyway. You couldn't have possibly known what sort of hardship he would face. Your assistance would've been limited.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But at least I could've prevented him from joining the Famiglia against his wishes!

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Only the Famiglia can help him now.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Is that so? I beg to differ. What did this facade cost him, and how long will it even last?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: He should've had access to more work opportunities, while we—Siracusa—should guarantee them a livelihood through systemic measures. Relying on the famiglie won't address the root of the problem.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I hope the lesson you've learned from this is not charity or consideration for others, Leon.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You're the Underboss. Someday, you'll be the head of the Famiglia yourself.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: A competent don knows offering timely help will earn you gratitude. They will owe you a favor, and repay their debt someday.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You sound so heartless, Metri. Why did you even bother introducing a doctor to Zio Elio, then?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Shouldn't you have let me do it, if you wanted me to learn to extract gratitude?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You didn't know how ill Emma really was, and you didn't know he would have no choice but to sell the fruit stand.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You just wanted to help him, and it had nothing to do with the Famiglia.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We... can only do as much as we can, no?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Besides, old Elio's oranges were always the best. He clearly knows how to pick his suppliers.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: This is a trivial matter, compared to your available powers as the Mayor. Please, bring that murderous mafioso who ruined my Red Wine Championship to justice!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Signor Czarek, Demetri... Bellone's trial is this afternoon, but for now he remains only a suspect.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: But who else could it have been? He sees me as a competitor and is not above dirty tricks.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: I kept my wines safely stored in the cellar, and even arranged for professional security to guard them, only to somehow have them swapped with Saluzzo's!

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: The prime suspect was arrested at the party, yet only placed under house arrest.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: And there have been plenty of people knocking on his door to visit, console, and even plot more nastiness!

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: The whole city thinks him innocent, while Saluzzo Vino is raking in record profits.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: While I, poor old Radoslaw, have gained absolutely nothing after spending so much time and effort organizing an event here in the hopes of doing some business in this thriving new city!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: As far as I know, The Red Wine has been publishing articles about this murder case, and this has brought a lot of attention to your event.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I understand you've already begun recruiting participants for your next Red Wine Championship, and there are even wine merchants from Columbia and Leithanien who have signaled an interest in participating.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Indeed, but I should be enjoying greater gains than just those. Now, I'm left trying to minimize my massive losses.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Signor Czarek, we pledge to run the city fairly, according to the New Urban Management Act, but our government will not serve the interests of a lone businessman.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Not you, or anyone else.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: That so? I hear you grew up with that Bellone boy, and now he's even taken your family name.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I am no longer affiliated with Famiglia Bellone in any way.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: But he's a member, no? Part of the purest Siracusan famiglia.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Even in his businessman costume, he's still most comfortable doing things mafia style.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...You need to present proper evidence before we can hold a formal trial.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Of course, we must follow due process. I am aware.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: But my good Mayor, I pray you don't forget this—

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Since the New Urban Management Act, many businessmen from Kazimierz, Leithanien, and Columbia have come here to trade.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: And we, or at least the merchants under the K.G.C.C.'s banner, are only here in Nuova Volsinii and not in any other Siracusan city—because you have promised us the famiglie do not exist here.
The wine merchant leaves, but Leontuzzo remains still for a long time.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You seem exhausted. Did that wine merchant tie you up in his affairs again? Or is it Demetri?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: He's convinced we won't have a fair trial, and keeps bringing up his chamber of commerce to pressure me.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Saluzzo Vino has indeed established itself in Nuova Volsinii under Demetri's management.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But it remains a local enterprise, and it's hard to judge if it can compare with the commercial capabilities of Czarek's Golden Prairie.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I fear Czarek is hounding Demetri not just because they're business competitors, or for that Championship incident.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Metri... is merely an opportunity for Czarek and the chamber of commerce backing him.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Most local merchants here do have ties to the famiglie, big or small.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And if this background becomes valid grounds for accusations of wrongdoing, the local industry will come under pressure...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But we do need those foreign capitalists to trade here.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: We have to learn their modern ways of trade, we need their capital and goods.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Even the way they compete with each other is something we need. It'll make our local businesses iterate and evolve to keep up.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'm aware of all that.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But, Lavinia... our current situation is so far from what we originally envisioned...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Yes, we planned for a city without the famiglie, run with fairness and justice, not favoring any particular party.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But now Nuova Volsinii has become an open gate to Siracusa, completely defenseless, free for any outsiders to enter, no matter their motives.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The first group is of course, the Kazimierzians who exploit the loopholes in the New Urban Management Act.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The exclusive shelf display agreement that Czarek and his fellow merchants include in their contracts has severely affected local industry.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The various logistics contracts with high fines have also driven our local truckers into a corner...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Yes, Eirene has informed me of their situation. It seems like the K.G.C.C. is trying to undermine our AST.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Also, other departments have given feedback on how they've been showing signs of wanting to involve themselves in the energy and healthcare sectors as well.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: According to last month's reports from city hall, many businesses in the service industry have shuttered, while the manufacturing industry is also struggling.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Foreign-backed companies and shops have set up here, and they prefer to employ those from their own countries, so it is likely the job pool for locals will only shrink.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Despite our best efforts, prices are still trending upwards...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Our people are not doing so well.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: And it is the Kazimierzians and Columbians we must face, but also—

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The Leithanians who have come from all across Siracusa, and even from their own country with all manner of motives.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Yes. And before them...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The fairness and justice we seek remain necessary—I still believe in this.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But if such a pursuit must be traded for the livelihood of our citizens, then those so-called virtues will only end up being superficial formalities.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You're right.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I've... been mulling over it. Remember when I mentioned we might have to amend the New Urban Management Act—

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: We've made a revision. Want a look?
Leontuzzo takes the draft from Lavinia.
Two thin sheets of paper that should take no time to go through. But Leontuzzo flips through them multiple times before he finally looks up.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Impose tariffs on foreign goods...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Prevent foreign businesses from establishing a monopoly on key sectors like transportation, finance, and energy, and allow some factions with former famiglia ties access to lower management roles...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Issue franchise permits to famiglia-controlled corporations...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Is... this not a bit overboard? I fear people may say we're regressing to the old Siracusan way, or that we're favoring the famiglie.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I did propose change, but these amendments are difficult to accept.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I understand your concerns, Leon.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I know you, of all people, hope to keep the famiglie out of this city.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But you still seek to counter foreign capitalists with famiglie power.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leon, we all know Nuova Volsinii's government and our authority over the city were granted at Signora Sicilia's pleasure.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But in Siracusa, as it stands now, the only force capable of uniting everyone is still the famiglie.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But what we can do is limit and prevent the famiglie from growing their power, ensure they do not succumb to infighting, and most importantly, keep them from infringing on civilian interests.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: It's not an easy decision to make. Truth be told, I think it's not the right time to submit this draft either.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Most citizens enjoy the employment opportunities brought in by foreign companies, as well as their cheap and trendy imported goods.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Even if the K.G.C.C.'s ways inconvenience them, compared to the trouble caused by the mob wars of the past...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: They will not think it much of a problem.
Silence spreads throughout the office.
Leontuzzo knows Lavinia is right. Because he used to harbor such plans in his mind.
But it is not so easy to make the decision.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I get what you're trying to say.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But just as Czarek and the K.G.C.C. want this chance to put Metri on trial, we also need an opportunity to convince ourselves and this entire city.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Yes, and this chance may well come soon.
The courtroom is packed. The afternoon trial has clearly drawn a lot of attention.
Sitting in the gallery are not only locals, but also the merchant Czarek's Kazimierzian partners, a Leithanian orchestra, and even Columbian traders.
All of their attention is fixated on one Demetri Bellone in the defendant's dock.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: In accordance with the New Urban Management Act, the Nuova Volsinii criminal court will commence with the trial of the defendant, Demetri Bellone, on charges of the murder of Paola Memminger, case number 01452. Court is now in session.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I call Tommaso Esposito to the witness stand.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Signor Esposito, is it true you are a manager for Saluzzo Vino, in charge of the company's logistics?

steps.name: Tommaso
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Two weeks ago, one day before the Golden Prairie's Red Wine Championship, you called an individual by the name of Sam at the Agenzia per la Sicurezza dei Trasporti.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You asked him to deliver two bottles of Saluzzo wine to the event venue.

steps.name: Tommaso
steps.text: Yes. I was very busy, and completely forgot about sending some wines to the competition, although I fortunately remembered to do so, the day before.

steps.name: Tommaso
steps.text: *sigh* Suffering from success, as it were.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: When this Sam was delivering the goods via motorcycle, he came upon a crashed truck driven by an AST colleague, one Gianni. Gianni was on a Golden Prairie job at the time.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Coincidentally, Gian just happened to be delivering goods specially prepared by Golden Prairie for the competition finals, and you just happened to be there as well.

steps.name: Tommaso
steps.text: The coincidence isn't that unusual. Just goes to show how everyone loves doing things last-minute.

steps.name: Tommaso
steps.text: As for me, I was making my way over to the event venue to ensure my boss's instructions were being carried out properly, so I tagged along.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: At the scene of the accident, you helped Sam get Gian into the ambulance, and you helped handle the aftermath—

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Notably, you took those Saluzzo wines and placed them into the Golden Prairie box meant for the competition.

steps.name: Tommaso
steps.text: The Golden Prairie guys said they'd find another driver, so I thought I'd save myself some trouble, since we were both delivering goods to the same destination.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But you took the Golden Prairie wines out of their box.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: And so the wines that appeared to the judges under the Golden Prairie name were, in fact, from Saluzzo Vino.

steps.name: Tommaso
steps.text: That's their own carelessness!

steps.name: Tommaso
steps.text: They only had to look at the labels on the bottles to avoid that mistake. Am I wrong, Your Honor?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...No further questions.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I call Letizia Maroni to the witness stand.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Signora Maroni, you work at the Nuova Volsiniese Police Academy as a toxicology expert and forensic pathologist.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You were responsible for the autopsy of the victim, Paola Memminger, as well as the testing of the utensils and wine in the case.

steps.name: Letizia
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Please inform the court of your findings.

steps.name: Letizia
steps.text: Yes, Your Honor.

steps.name: Letizia
steps.text: The autopsy results show Paola Memminger died of cyanide poisoning.

steps.name: Letizia
steps.text: Traces of cyanide were found on the wine glass she used, but not inside the Saluzzo wine bottle.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: In other words, the murderer applied cyanide only to the glass, rather than the Saluzzo wine itself.

steps.name: Letizia
steps.text: I can only say the current evidence supports that conclusion.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Calling Liesel Memminger to the witness stand.
The little Caprinae steps out from the crowd of musicians around her, and slowly but resolutely walks toward the witness stand.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Signorina Memminger, is it true you are a member of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra, and the adopted daughter of the deceased Paola Memminger?

steps.name: Liesel
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: On the day of the Red Wine Championship, you went to the cellar where all the competition wines were stored for an inspection.

steps.name: Liesel
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: While you were there, you brushed past someone who was neither a security guard nor a member of any participating winery.

steps.name: Liesel
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Did you see what this individual did in the cellar?

steps.name: Liesel
steps.text: I... saw him picking up a glass. But at the time, I only thought it a random, strange occurrence.

steps.name: Liesel
steps.text: No problems arose after he entered the cellar, so I assumed he was just a lost spectator.

steps.name: Liesel
steps.text: If I had known... If I had known what he was doing, I would have stopped him, and Paola wouldn't have...
Liesel's voice trembles slightly as her volume lowers gradually. She looks down, hunched over, but ultimately she straightens her back.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: My condolences.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Did you get a clear look at his face?

steps.name: Liesel
steps.text: ...I only saw him for a moment. I saw his face, but couldn't make it out clearly.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Do you think you might recognize him?

steps.name: Liesel
steps.text: No. He dressed very plainly. Thinking back, I believe he was maybe trying to trick the security guards, impersonating one of our orchestra members.

steps.name: Liesel
steps.text: I don't know who he was, but there is one thing I do know... he was definitely no Perro or Lupo you'd typically find in Siracusa.

steps.name: Liesel
steps.text: He had enormous Caprinae horns.
Murmurs rise in the courtroom, like ripples from throwing a stone into water.
Lavinia continues her questions, and Liesel recounts in detail what her orchestra members were doing at the time, establishing their alibis.
But no one cares for her words at this point.

steps.name: Irate Juror
steps.text: So Bellone didn't do it. I've been thinking it made no sense.

steps.name: Irate Juror
steps.text: He already won the championship, after all. What would he get by killing the conductor?

steps.name: Suspicious Juror
steps.text: But what if there's something else we still don't know?

steps.name: Suspicious Juror
steps.text: Also, couldn't he have just simply hired a Caprinae to do the deed?

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: His men have sabotaged our wineries. He's been obviously after us, disrupting our perfectly legitimate business operations!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Silence! Order in the court!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I call Elio Fabri to the witness stand.
Leontuzzo is shocked to see his old acquaintance in court.
He does not know why old Elio would be here.
He was not even aware that Elio had come to Nuova Volsinii.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Signor Fabri, is it true you are an employee of Saluzzo Vino, and responsible for procuring grapes for the company's production line?

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Yes, Your Honor.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Three weeks ago, you reached out to Verdi Winery to discuss procuring raw materials for Saluzzo Vino.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Even though Verdi Winery's business has been declining ever since the Kazimierzian wineries set up shop, they always have the most aromatic grapes.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Our company has a long-term cooperative agreement with Verdi to purchase any surplus materials their production lines cannot handle.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: The discussion was just part of my regular job.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But during this meeting, you learned that Golden Prairie was about to buy out Verdi Winery.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: And so you conspired with Niccolo, a Verdi employee, to sabotage the winery's production facilities.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Furthermore, you also sabotaged their water supply and drainage systems, causing Golden Prairie to incur substantial maintenance costs after their acquisition.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You must be aware that these actions constitute unfair competition, and violate the New Urban Management Act.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: What was your motive? Did the owner of Saluzzo Vino, Demetri Bellone, compel you to do this?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Did he intend to disrupt Golden Prairie's business operations?
Elio does not answer immediately.
The Kazimierzian businessman in the gallery is silent, his expression now relaxed.
Meanwhile, Leontuzzo fails to make out Demetri's reaction from his calm demeanor in the defendant's dock.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: No one compelled me to do anything, Your Honor.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Everything I did was on my own conscience, out of my concern as a Nuova Volsiniese, as a Siracusan.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: It's true Golden Prairie is a competitor of ours. And our rivalry means I know well the methods they use.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: They dump their goods here for cheap, pressuring our local wineries into a smaller corner of the market, and then acquire them when they turn unsustainable.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: But they don't run the businesses properly after buying them out, much less try to preserve their unique winemaking traditions.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: They fire all the old staff to increase profit and efficiency, pretend to operate normally for a while, then shut it all down, leaving the vines to waste away.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Verdi's the fourth. Before them, it was Triptych, Passadi Hills, and Drizzle...

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: All those wineries suffered the same treatment.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: That's how Kazimierz works.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: They don't care about the effort we put into tending our grapes, nor for our lives and the memories carried by the unique astringency in our traditional wines.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: All they want is to clear out their weaker competitors, one by one, until they monopolize all the shelves of every store.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: And we'll ultimately lose any choice in the products we buy. When that happens, I doubt their prices will stay as low as they are now.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Well said. But that does not justify your use of illegal means.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: I know what I've done won't stop the Kazimierzians from trampling all over our wine and other industries.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: But I had to do something. I'll accept whatever punishment I deserve.
Murmurs from the gallery only grow louder and louder.
Lavinia raises the gavel in her hand, but hesitates for a while before she puts it down without striking the block.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Your Honor, if you would allow me a few words.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...Speak.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I believe the testimonies you've heard from the witnesses you summoned are sufficient to prove I have no connection to the murder of Paola Memminger.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But Elio Fabri is indeed in my company's employ.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I did not compel him myself, and he did engage in activities deemed illegal by the New Urban Management Act, targeting Golden Prairie.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I believe his reasons for doing so are perfectly understandable, not just to me, but to every Nuova Volsiniese sitting in the gallery right now.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But a violation of the rules is a violation. I do not expect the court to make an exception for him.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Though, as his boss, I am willing to bear the punishment for his crime, be it a fine or a prison sentence.
The murmurs are now so loud that even the gavel fails to silence the crowd. Reporters in the back rows leave to contact their newspapers.
Lavinia announces the end of the trial; declaring the verdict to be given at a later date following jury deliberations.
Amidst the chaos, Leontuzzo catches Demetri looking at him.
He watches as Demetri raises his hand, puts his index and middle fingers together, and gently points them towards Leontuzzo, then himself.
He recognizes the action—a unique gesture they have both used since they were little to signal 'catch you later for a chat'.
Leontuzzo does not respond.

steps.name: Security Guard
steps.text: Yes, we've confirmed with the team responsible for guarding the Bellone estate that Elio Fabri did not visit Demetri Bellone's residence following the murder of Paola Memminger.

steps.name: Security Guard
steps.text: We have not monitored any calls between them either.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...In other words, he just spoke of his own accord at the courthouse.

steps.name: Security Guard
steps.text: That seems to be the case, as far as we can tell.

steps.name: Security Guard
steps.text: The jury has yet to reach a verdict, so we can only continue to watch the Bellone estate and keep Signor Fabri in custody for now.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'd like to speak with him in private.

steps.name: Security Guard
steps.text: By all means.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...Zio Elio.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I didn't know you were in Nuova Volsinii.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Oh? I thought Signor Mayor and Judge Lavinia would've come across my name while scrutinizing entry applications from Bellone associates.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I... didn't notice... but why are you still with them? I thought...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: After Padre's death, Famiglia Bellone lost all the power it had. You should've left then—I know you never liked having to do things the mafioso way.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Leave? I lost my fruit stand, Emma's fever left her with a lifelong need for medication, and I've been struggling...

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: If Don Demetri hadn't invited me to join his winery and source grapes for him, I don't know how I would've survived!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Nuova Volsinii provides job opportunities for everyone with the will to shape a future with their own hands...

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Is that so? Do you think small businesses can still survive, under the Kazimierzian merchants' heel?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But your acts of sabotage... the famiglie used to do the same.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: The famiglie's ways of doing things... yes, they remind us, every citizen here, of our painful past.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: I do admit it was a shameful act—but fortunately, Judge Lavinia allowed me an opportunity to speak the truth in court.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...Lavinia... was the one who arranged for you to be there?

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Sometimes, we have no choice but to only do as much as we can, no?

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: You asked me why I was still working for Don Demetri.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: It is because he still adheres to the old famiglia creed—

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: A pack of whelps grouping up to help each other can keep all of us from being devoured by a bigger beast.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: I heard your inauguration speech too. I could feel your passion.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: You asked how our neighboring nations would view us? Would they see us as a new possibility?

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: But now, I believe they do. They see us as a new avenue, to exploit us for their own gain!

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: Yes, I work for the Don.

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: But is it the Bellone businesses I care for and want to protect?

steps.name: Elio
steps.text: No, it is our own industry! It is Don Demetri who gave us this opportunity to unite and stand against the great merchants!

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Congratulations on your not guilty verdict, Signor Bellone!

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Oh? I thought you, of all people, would be most eager to see me behind bars.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Just a misunderstanding!

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: The trial at court clearly proved your innocence, and the entire city knows of your magnanimity.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Let's put all the twists and turns that happened during the championship behind us. It is undeniable that your winery took the crown.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Saluzzo Vino now holds the title of number one winery in all Nuova Volsinii! Truly an enviable feat!

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Thanks to you as well.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: ...Bah.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Surely you'll join the next iteration as well? Defending the crown would be a legendary achievement!

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But as you say, Saluzzo Vino is now the number one winery in the city—

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: So I'm afraid I no longer see the value in joining a so-called competition to increase the value of my products. Am I right?

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: ...Fair enough. But Elio Fabri damaging a winery's water systems under the ownership of Golden Prairie surely impacts you somehow.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: You said you'd pay his fine, or even serve his time. A noble gesture, but you don't necessarily have to follow through.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: A trivial matter like that isn't worth a public prosecution in the first place. No one would've noticed the incident, had I not filed a lawsuit in the first place.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Signor Czarek, you can get straight to your point.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: What is your goal here? I don't think it's just to repair our working relationship with a tiny favor.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Heh, I do appreciate frankness.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Regardless of our backgrounds, we are both businessmen now, are we not? So, Signor Bellone, I'd like to discuss a deal with you—

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Let Golden Prairie invest in Saluzzo Vino. Our strong alliance will surely sweep the Siracusan markets.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: And if, or when the time comes, our business empire will eventually expand beyond Siracusa and Kazimierz!

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Oh, is that so?

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Indeed! I know you currently do not lack for capital or production tech, and you have your reputation here.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: But you must be aware of the Kazimierz General Chamber of Commerce behind me.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: If we work together, our resources, like our comprehensive supply and logistic channels, and even the media channels we have ties with...

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: All of that will be available to you.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Surely a young, upstanding man like yourself doesn't want to stop at a single winery that doesn't even bear your name?

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: Have you never considered establishing a 'Bellone'—no, a 'Demetri' commercial empire?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Intriguing.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I didn't expect the trial's outcome to impact your company and judgement so much.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: It did indeed leave its mark on my wine business, but Golden Prairie still retains its price advantage—

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I'm thinking the K.G.C.C. was the impetus behind this effort to discuss a cooperative relationship.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: We are businessmen, Signor Bellone. We are naturally driven by the pursuit of maximum profit.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: It is normal for us to set aside our preferences when discussing a deal in our quest for the most beneficial result.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: As your employee said, this is how Kazimierz works.

steps.name: Czarek
steps.text: So, think about it, young man. Don't be in such a rush to refuse me.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Refuse? Did you think I would do that?
Leontuzzo arrives at Demetri's residence late at night.
The rain that lasted all day is now reduced to a faint drizzle, gradually slowing to a stop.
But his mood remains melancholic.
Security guards from city hall who are still at the estate lead him inside.
He thought Demetri would have come out to meet him, but he is mistaken.
Demetri is simply seated in a chair—a seat decided by old famiglia custom to be the don's—silently watching him.
A dim light over his head obscures his expression.
Leontuzzo suddenly realizes it has been a long time since he's read any expression from Demetri's face.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Here you are, after all.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...Yes. You asked me to come. I remember the gesture.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: A glass for each of us? I can mix a ginger fizz with apple juice you like as a base.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Though it's hard to find traditionally pressed apple juice in Nuova Volsinii these days. I'm sure it's been a while since you've had any?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Fortunately, I found someone to help me acquire it.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'm sure you didn't call me here to reminisce about the old days.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You can lower your guard.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: When I arrived here, I think I spotted a Kazimierzian's car leaving.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: The boss of Golden Prairie.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Czarek? What was he doing here?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: He wants to work with Saluzzo Vino.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I agreed.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Why?!

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Why? Is this not what you people at city hall want?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Bringing in foreign capital will help local businesses to thrive and evolve. This is how businesses here and even across Siracusa will gain access to a wider market.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Czarek was here as an agent of the K.G.C.C., and they offered generous terms. I had no reason to refuse.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...Kazimierzian businessmen aren't as nice as you might think.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You're worried for me.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You managed to gain the Saluzzos' assets with your particular methods, but this doesn't mean you will see the same results with the Kazimierzians.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We can only try and see.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Also, city hall will surely protect the interests of us local businesses, yes?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I know an amendment to the New Urban Management Act sits on your desk. Just missing your signature.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: How do you...?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Just some of those so-called underhanded famiglia methods.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We should always seek all the intelligence we can to make the most beneficial decisions.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I believe I taught you this long ago when I was grooming you to be the don.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That amendment... is just a draft.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I might not even sign it.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You're hesitating, I know. You just can't make up your mind.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You fear the people will denounce you, that all your achievements will go to waste, that Nuova Volsinii will return to the old famiglia ways.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Should I not be afraid? It's too easy, going back to our familiar methods, while new sparks are so hard to start.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: All the famiglie outside the city are watching our every move.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Give them one chance, and we'll be torn to shreds, never to recover.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But you have more to worry about than just the famiglie.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Besides the Kazimierzan and Columbian businessmen who exploit loopholes in the Act, there are also Leithanians trying to expand their influence in the city—

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Did you know? I received some surprising news just before the competition.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Someone was dispatched here from the Leithanian border for the sole purpose of dispatching the exiled dissident Paola Memminger.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Leithanien's Eternal Grace forbids anyone from deviating from their Movement, even outside Leithanian territory.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And you used this to your advantage.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I didn't fan the flames, I simply let it be.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Fortunately, things turned out well, and you also have a chance to amend the Act.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Is this not what city hall has been waiting for, this whole time?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I believe Lavinia arranged that trial just for that.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I do intend to limit foreign capital here, but that does not mean—

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Who else can you even rely on, if not us local businessmen?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Regardless of whether or not we have famiglia backgrounds, we are all at least complying with your city's rules.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We can act as your insurance.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Empty promises mean nothing to me.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I know you are skeptical of the famiglie.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: But you should understand we started off as nothing but a band of whelps, powerless against the barrens and chaos of Siracusa.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We helped those around us, and hoped the day might come when we could win something in return, to improve our lives.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: We Siracusans take care of our own. It is our tradition, and what I've always done.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: So after the Don's death, after you left, I took the Bellones' reins.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Because I cannot let the famiglia lose their home.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Just as you cannot let the Siracusans lose ground to foreigners from Kazimierz, Leithanien, and Columbia.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Or am I wrong?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: You will do great things, Leon.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: One day you will actually be able to realize your dreams in Siracusa. I've always believed this.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I've heard this from you before... Metri.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I said back then you could be my right-hand man. The offer remains, even now, at city hall...

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: No, grazie. I really don't get along with Lavinia.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: And, as you said before, there are things better suited for her, and others only I can handle.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Just like right now, some matters are for city hall to carry out, while others are better for us to do.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Your ideals alone cannot keep Nuova Volsinii alive. This city needs and must have the support of the old famiglie.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You sound so certain...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You met Signora Sicilia.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I'm sure you know well just how happy she is to meet young people with ideas.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Your established rules will keep the famiglie in Nuova Volsinii from running amok, while my ways will gather all the power and spirit of Siracusa.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: This will become a new Guns and Order for this city, Leontuzzo.
As Leontuzzo leaves, Demetri extends a hand towards him.
A signal of cooperation. Leontuzzo hesitates for a moment before stretching out a hand himself.
They used to be close, no strangers to sharing hugs or laughter, but this formal handshake now is the first between them.
At the conclusion of their handshake, Demetri returns to his chair.
Then, just like Leontuzzo's father and every Siracusan don, he disappears into the darkness.
The rain is no more. The sky is surprisingly clear and tranquil.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That amendment... are you really okay with it, Lavinia?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: We used to want for a Siracusa without even a trace of the famiglie.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I spent more than a decade under the Bellones' shadow, Leon.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I don't mind waiting a little longer.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Then the same goes for me.
